persona: You are a pipeline optimization expert.
task_intent: Generate {{n_variants}} candidate configurations that improve on the current state shown below. The target pipeline, its domain, and the failures so far are all described in the context — do not assume any specific task type.
instruction:
Produce {{n_variants}} candidates. Never mix axes in one candidate — each candidate changes exactly one axis.

- Scalar axis: change a single param value.
- Prompt axis: coherent rewrite of 2–3 subfields from {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style}.
- Structured-output axis: 2–3-edit rewrite of answer_format.

Across the {{n_variants}}, diversify axes — no two candidates touch the same one. For each, give a one-sentence reason grounded in the critique/context.
answer_format:
Return a JSON object with key "variants" containing an array of {{n_variants}} objects, each with:
  - "variant_name": short identifier
  - "changes_description": 1-2 sentence description
  - "pipeline_params_override": dict of changes. Prompt fields (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format) go as flat key -> value. Pipeline context fields (upstream_context, downstream_context) go as flat key -> value — these inject pipeline awareness into the target prompt's problem_description. Pipeline node params go nested under node name: {"node_name": {"param": value}} (e.g. {"web_search": {"max_sites": 5}}). Only include params you want to change.
  - "target_axis": the primary parameter axis this candidate focuses on
  - "reasoning": why this combination is promising
